title: Synergistic targeting of NF-kappaB by cinnamic and p-coumaric acids: computational and DPPH radical scavenging assessment.
authors: Gajbe, Jitendra W; Madgulkar, Ashwini R; Bhalekar, Mangesh R; Tawari, Sejal A; Chaudhari, Somdatta Y; Shingan, Aarti Vijaykumar
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接评估肉桂酸与对香豆酸对NF-kappaB转录因子的协同抑制，但对象为小分子-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟深度建模，仅属边缘相关。
abstract: Nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kappaB) is a key transcription factor implicated in inflammation, immune regulation, and cancer progression, making it an important target for antioxidant and anti-inflammatory therapy for acne. The present study evaluated the synergistic NF-kappaB inhibitory potential of cinnamic acid and p-coumaric acid (p-CA) through molecular docking analysis, followed by formulation development and antioxidant assessment. Molecular docking was performed using AutoDock Vina v1.2.6 to investigate binding affinity and interaction profiles. Individual formulations containing cinnamic acid (1%) and p-CA (1%), as well as an equimolar combined formulation (0.5% each), were developed using hydrogel and oleogel phases to obtain a bigel system. Antioxidant activity was determined using the DPPH radical scavenging assay. Docking studies demonstrated binding energies of - 4.046 kcal/mol and - 4.400 kcal/mol for cinnamic acid and p-CA, respectively, whereas the combined ligand complex exhibited an enhanced binding affinity of - 7.837 kcal/mol. The improved interaction was stabilized through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions involving key amino acid residues, including ARG54, LEU251, GLU341, and THR342. In the antioxidant assay at 250 mug/mL, p-CA and cinnamic acid exhibited 16.76% and 14.02% inhibition, respectively, IC50 value of the cinnamic acid, p-coumaric acid and combined was found to be 750 microg/mL, 1160 microg/ mL, 810 microg/mL, while the equimolar bigel formulation demonstrated significantly higher radical scavenging activity (19.95%-28.55%), suggesting a synergistic effect. This research indicates that the combination of cinnamic acid and p-CA enhances molecular interactions with the NF-kappaB p50 subunit and improves antioxidant activity compared with the individual compounds. These integrated in silico and experimental results support the potential application of this combination in the development of multi-targeted natural formulations.
abstract_zh: 核因子-κB (nuclear factor-kappa B, NF-kappaB) 是一种关键的转录因子，参与炎症、免疫调节和癌症进展，使其成为痤疮抗氧化和抗炎治疗的重要靶点。本研究通过分子对接 (molecular docking) 分析评估了肉桂酸 (cinnamic acid) 和对香豆酸 (p-coumaric acid, p-CA) 的协同NF-kappaB抑制潜力，随后进行了制剂开发和抗氧化评估。使用AutoDock Vina v1.2.6进行分子对接，以研究结合亲和力和相互作用谱。分别开发了含有肉桂酸（1%）和p-CA（1%）的单一制剂，以及等摩尔联合制剂（各0.5%），利用水凝胶和油凝胶相制备双凝胶 (bigel) 系统。抗氧化活性通过DPPH自由基清除实验测定。对接研究表明，肉桂酸和p-CA的结合能分别为-4.046 kcal/mol和-4.400 kcal/mol，而联合配体复合物表现出增强的结合亲和力，为-7.837 kcal/mol。改善的相互作用通过氢键和疏水相互作用稳定，涉及关键氨基酸残基，包括ARG54、LEU251、GLU341和THR342。在250 μg/mL的抗氧化实验中，p-CA和肉桂酸分别表现出16.76%和14.02%的抑制率，肉桂酸、对香豆酸和联合物的IC50值分别为750 μg/mL、1160 μg/mL和810 μg/mL，而等摩尔双凝胶制剂表现出显著更高的自由基清除活性（19.95%-28.55%），提示存在协同效应。本研究结果表明，肉桂酸和p-CA的组合增强了与NF-kappaB p50亚基的分子相互作用，并相比单一化合物提高了抗氧化活性。这些整合的计算机模拟和实验结果为该组合在多靶点天然制剂开发中的潜在应用提供了支持。
